terms.gloss: regulate, govern; temper, mix in due measure
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 1.2: rem pūblicam īnstitūtīs et lēgibus temperāre (Lewis & Short)
Hor. C. 3.19.6: quis aquam temperet ignibus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To keep things in due proportion: a state by laws, a bath by heating it, the year by its seasons. Intransitive temperāre (+ dat.) is to restrain oneself or spare.

evidence: Cic. Rep. 6.26: deus, quī regit et moderātur et movet id corpus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To keep within a measure (modus) and so to guide or govern; with the dative, to restrain (linguae moderārī). See control.

terms.gloss: to provide by law, make a rule that
terms.comment: Regulation by statute: lēge cautum est nē …, the law lays down that … not (see rule-regulation).

phrases.latin: Tempera aquam, nē nimis calida sit.
phrases.english: Adjust the water so it isn’t too hot.

sources: Lewis & Short: tempero · Lewis & Short: moderor · Lewis & Short: caveo
